deepdive.thesis: M M Forgings Limited is a leading manufacturer of steel forgings with a strong presence in the domestic and export markets, but faces challenges due to its dependence on the cyclical auto industry and moderate capital structure.

open.item: H1 EBITDA 19% (17.5% operational) vs 21%; EBITDA/ton INR 38,000 vs 40,500; margins expected to only improve from these levels if sales have bottomed.
Domestic addressable market shrinking as multi-axle vehicles give way to tractor-trailers (fewer front axles); domestic CV static, ~+/-2%.
US 50% tariff borne by customers (CIF contracts); expected absorbed until ~March, then resourcing/renegotiation likely; margins could pressure if sustained.
Net debt to come down ~INR 50-75 Crores via inventory compression; scope for at least INR 50 Cr inventory reduction.
Converting rupee loans to forex to cut interest; H1 interest INR 39 Cr; targeting FY26 interest within INR 70 Cr, run-rate INR 50-60 Cr (saves ~INR 12 Cr/yr).
H2 FY26 revenue expected ~INR 750-800 Crores, taking full-year close to previous year's level (give or take a few percent).
Plan to add wind/solar green power (from ~3 cr to up to 10 cr units) to insulate against 5%/yr TN power hikes; ~150 bps EBITDA benefit, likely from next year.
US Class VIII truck market seen as bottom (Q2 worst); customer restocking from November, reasonable levels by June 2026.
Abhinava Rizel acquired first customer (~INR 20-30 Cr annual potential); sample parts to be delivered end-Nov 2025, then production; also commercializing controllers.
Sales expected to grow by at least INR 300 Crores in next 12-18 months; decline reversing to growth from FY27 onwards.
FY27 to add 15,000-20,000 tons capacity via 16,500t press plus a ~4,000t forging line, pushing capacity to ~140,000 tons; targeting 80,000-90,000 tons output.
FY26 capex ~INR 170 Cr (INR 100 Cr H1, ~INR 70 Cr H2); FY27 capex ~INR 100-120 Cr; ~INR 70 Cr investment remaining at fag end of expansion cycle.
Order book of ~INR 300 Crores revenue, of which ~INR 200 Crores expected to realize in FY27.
Net debt ~INR 850-855 Crores declared as peak debt; no more borrowing intended, hold at these levels; no significant reduction next 2 years (store cash / cut working capital instead).
New export customer acquisitions expected to add at least INR 100 Crores of export sales in FY27 and FY28.
Abhinava Rizel/EV powertrain (incl controllers) long-term revenue of Rs.1,000-2,000 Crores over 7-10 year horizon.
Scheme of Amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiary DVS Industries Private Limited with the Company, pending NCLT approval, with appointed date 01 April 2024.

The Company has embarked on a strategic transition towards 100% green energy, entering into long-term arrangements with captive power generating units and has started consuming green power from Q4FY26 onwards.
Strategic transition towards 100% green energy, with visible improvements in operating performance expected from the upcoming FY.
Enabling resolution approved for raising funds up to an aggregate amount of ₹600 crores via QIP or other permissible modes.

FY2024 production/sales targeted at 85,000-90,000 tonnes (sales +/-5%), from ~76,000 tonnes production last year.
EBITDA per tonne guided flattish at ~Rs.35,000 for full year; 19% EBITDA margin reasonably on track (needs push to 36-37k/tonne).
H1 EBITDA 19% (17.5% operational) vs 21%; EBITDA/ton INR 38,000 vs 40,500; margins expected to only improve from these levels if sales have bottomed.
